PLACF ULtra violet lighting in all halls, rooms, bathrooms, throughout the city, fire house, schools, police. Be an example to the community. Reagan, the greatest leader is not who does the greatest things, but who gets the people to do the greatest things. Ultra violet lamps are placed in all public buildings, city and county, and schools as an effective anti bacterial and anti viral prophylaxis. UV light is an inexpensive solution to reduce the spread of pathogens in air and public places. UV works by radiation which denatures the proteins in virus or bacteria, similar to giving the microscopic bacteria a bad sunburn. UV is dry and will not stain cloth or wood. It can turn on in bath rooms or halls when empty, and turn off when rooms are occupied. UV works on distance to target, time of radiation and power of the light source. Leave them on over the weekend, nights, and vacations. Ultraviolet (UV) radiation is a form of non-ionizing radiation that is emitted by both natural and artificial sources. There are both benefits and risks to UV radiation. You should always protect yourself from over-exposure to reduce your risk of sunburn, premature aging, and skin cancer.

The basics. Ultraviolet (UV) radiation is a form of non-ionizing radiation that is emitted by the sun and artificial sources. The beneficial effects of UV radiation include the production of a vital nutrient, vitamin D. However, overexposure may present risks. Sunburn, premature aging, and skin cancer are all risks to overexposure. UV sterilization has a wide variety of applications including: Water treatment to disinfect drinking water; Surface sterilization to disinfect laboratory benches and high-contact surfaces in healthcare settings; Medical sterilization to disinfect medical equipment, patient rooms or personal protective equipment (PPE).

UVC light sterilizes surfaces by killing or inactivating microorganisms. The mechanism involves disrupting the genetic material of the microorganism. To begin, the UVC light photons emitted are absorbed by the microorganism. This triggers chemical reactions within the microorganism. Covalent bonds form between adjacent thymine-thymine molecules in DNA, and uracil-uracil molecules in RNA. The formation of these covalent bonds creates structural abnormalities in the DNA or RNA strands. Consequently, genetic replication and function is disrupted. With damaged DNA or RNA, microorganisms are unable to accurately replicate or successfully reproduce. This results in death or inactivation of the microorganism.

Utah traditionally ranks in the top 3 of 50 states (and DC) in major health categories, such as low cancer rates, and Health. This is great. Utah has only one medical school, at the University of Utah, and one osteopathic school in Ivins. Another is proposed for Provo. City council should petition for unlimited Homestead exemption in Utah. Adopt unlimited homestead protection for Utah homeowners. Homestead Protects homes against lawsuits, liability, & tax foreclosure. Present Utah homestead exemption law has a cap of $84K, while the median home in Utah is $500,000. Texas has NO Limit, and is luring population to move in. Under present Utah law, paying off the mortgage, free and clear, still leaves your home vulnerable to judgement for lawsuit.

https://www.findlaw.com/state/property-and-real-estate-laws/details-on-state-homestead-protections.html The federal exemption amount is $22,975 (as of 2015) and may be applied to burial plots and mobile homes as well as houses and condos. Additionally, married couples may double this exemption to $45,950. However, keep in mind that federal law requires a 40-month residency in the property prior to declaring homestead protection.

In Texas, every family and every single adult person is entitled to a homestead exempt from seizure passed on the claims of creditors, except for a pre-existing mortgage or lien. Texas homestead law protects qualifying real property from forced sale by general creditors, and courts have interpreted the laws broadly to help accomplish their goals. An urban homestead may be a home or a place of business, or both. There is no limit to the value of urban or rural homesteads, only to their size. Rural homesteads are limited to 200 acres for a family and 100 acres for a single adult, including improvements on the property. An urban homestead is limited to ten acres with improvements, which must be in adjacent lots. Creating homestead rights in a piece of property in Texas does not require a formalized legal process or the filing of a specific document. Creating a homestead is typically based on how owners use the land and whether they intend to claim the land as a permanent residence. While you do not have to actually occupy the property, you do need the right to possession of the property. By the same token, occupying and using a piece of land alone doesn't make it a homestead. Different types of usage of the property are required to establish urban and rural homesteads.

Utah Effective 5/14/2019 78B-5-503. Homestead exemption -- Definitions -- Excepted obligations -- Water rights and interests -- Conveyance -- Sale and disposition -- Propertyright for federal tax purposes. (2)(a) An individual is entitled to a homestead exemption consisting of property in this state in an amount not exceeding: (i) $5,000 in value if the property consists in whole or in part of property that is not the primary personal residence of the individual; or (ii) $42,000 in value if the property claimed is the primary personal residence of the individual. (b) If the property claimed as exempt is jointly owned, each joint owner is entitled to a homestead exemption, except that: (i) for property exempt under Subsection (2)(a)(i), the maximum exemption may not exceed $10,000 per household; or (ii) for property exempt under Subsection (2)(a)(ii), the maximum exemption may not exceed $84,000 per household.

A homestead is exempt from judicial lien and from levy, execution, or forced sale except for: (a) statutory liens for property taxes and assessments on the property; (b) security interests in the property and judicial liens for debts created for the purchase price of the property; (c) judicial liens obtained on debts created by failure to provide support or maintenance for dependent children; and (d) consensual liens obtained on debts created by mutual contract.

(4)(a) Except as provided in Subsection (4)(b), water rights and interests, either in the form of corporate stock or otherwise, owned by the homestead claimant are exempt from execution to the extent that those rights and interests are necessarily employed in supplying water to the homestead for domestic and irrigating purposes. (b) Those water rights and interests are not exempt from calls or assessments and sale by the corporations issuing the stock.

Utah Constitution. Article XXII of the Utah Constitution is entitled Miscellaneous and consists of four sections. Text of Section 1: Homestead exemption. The Legislature shall provide by statute for an exemption of a homestead, which may consist of one or more parcels of lands, together with the appurtenances and improvements thereon, from sale on execution.

comments.subject: Bike Park Construction
comments.comment:
Dear Members of the St. George City Council,

I am writing to encourage the City to prioritize experience and proven expertise when selecting a contractor for the design and construction of bike parks and pump tracks. I am concerned that the parks department does not have a clear understanding of the importance of hiring experience and qualified contractors who specialize in these types of facilities. While it may be tempting to award these projects to the lowest bidder, facilities of this nature require a highly specialized skill set that directly impacts safety, longevity, and overall community value.

Bike parks and pump tracks are not typical site construction projects. They demand a deep understanding of rider flow, grading precision, drainage design, soil composition, and user safety across a wide range of skill levels. Contractors who specialize in this type of work have refined these elements through years of focused experience, resulting in facilities that are both functional and enduring. Firms such as Velosolutions have established international reputations by consistently delivering high-quality tracks that attract users, host events, and require less ongoing maintenance. St. George is already a member of the Sourcewell purchasing cooperative and could hire them without need for an RFP and get our very own, amazing bike park!

By contrast, an inexperienced contractor—even with strong general construction capabilities—may lack the nuanced knowledge required for these projects. Small errors in shaping, compaction, or drainage can lead to poor ride quality, accelerated deterioration, increased maintenance costs, and potential safety hazards. Worse, their poor design and execution means they simply don't get used. A good example of this is Santa Clara's skatepark which was built without any knowledge and experience and is unusable for bikes, skateboards, and scooters. While good intentioned, in many cases municipalities that initially chose a low-bid, inexperienced builder ultimately face costly repairs or full reconstruction, negating any upfront savings. This is evidenced by the need to pave the Snake Hollow pump tracks. It also appears that this will be the case for the new Curly Hollow bike pump track. Both contracts were awarded to the same, inexperienced contractor. My hope is that it won't be the case for the upcoming Lizard Wash or future bike parks.

Investing in an experienced contractor is not simply about quality—it is also about long-term fiscal responsibility. A properly designed and constructed bike park will last longer, perform better, and serve a broader segment of the community. It becomes an asset that supports recreation, tourism, and public health, rather than a liability requiring frequent fixes.

St. George has an opportunity to create a standout facility that reflects the City's commitment to quality and active living. A great example of this is Washington's newly opened Wheels Park which has already been celebrated and praised nation-wide. Selecting a contractor with a proven track record will help ensure that this investment delivers lasting value to residents and visitors alike. Choosing the inexperienced low-bidder is a waste of tax payer funds.

Thank you for your time and consideration.

Matt Metcalf, Architect
